title: land waits for a finished headless worker's SessionEnd hook before refusing a live process in its worktree
goal: Found in SP-d3hybrlv: right after the headless worker of ST-7yahfn3j exited, land stopped at step branch naming a live python3 in its worktree (the session's own end hook, gone seconds later); a rerun landed. land waits at most 60 seconds for a process whose parent claude session has exited before refusing, and names it as a hook when it is one. backlog.py selfcheck and procs likewise tell a session-end hook's querylog.py distill (reparented to pid 1 while it delivers, seconds old) from an orphan a worker left: it is named as a hook in flight with its age and does not fail the orphans check while younger than 60 seconds (SP-flkl5gom close: selfcheck FAILed orphans on three 12-second-old distill processes from the operator's /clear, which finished on their own); a planted test proves a young distill process passes and an old stray process still fails.

gates.question: How long does land wait for a finished worker's session-end hook, and how young is a distill process that selfcheck names as a hook in flight?

notes: Merged from ST-5oruclxm (the bl_procs and bl_selfcheck half and its planted test) at the 2026-10-10 backlog triage; no premise change: grep distill in bl_procs.py and bl_selfcheck.py finds no match, and bl_land.release_worker_worktree refuses on any live_processes entry. Both -k selectors name tests yet to write: tests.py exits 2 until the work adds them (land_waits_hook in test_land_e2e.py, selfcheck_young_distill in test_backlog_portable.py). Orders after ST-xdyk2ugr, which edits land's start in the same file. Premise run at planning (2026-10-10): grep -c distill in _tools/bl_procs.py and _tools/bl_selfcheck.py prints 0 and 0, and release_worker_worktree returns its refusal on any live_processes entry with no wait: reproduces.
